added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own suite-delta arms, both complete and readable: after_suite (after-suite.log, revision 0bdce50f7b8116836e9844f0dc3da8eff304f4ce, 83-file head arm, '733 passed, 7 warnings in 310.27s', EXIT=0, failure_count 0) and baseline_suite (base-suite.log, revision 130812151dcd981f400fb9385c275d7c2e8690a7, same 83-file list, '733 passed, 7 warnings in 373.45s', EXIT=0, failure_count 0). findings.text: follow-on: `_codex_session_of_stream` re-implements the codex thread-id extraction the repository already owns at reckon/_backends.py:1314 (the codex backend's `_observe` sets `obs.session_id = event.get("thread_id")` on a `thread.started` record) and again at reckon/crew/metering.py:98-101. The loop at promotion_checks.py:205-209 already calls `_backends.observe_log` for the same `candidate` and holds `observation.session_id`, which is exactly that thread id, one statement before the helper is invoked, so the new 20-line function duplicates an available reading rather than extending its owner. Harmless at runtime (both read the same cached events), but it forks a capability the repository owns and is the reason this review scores reuse low.

follow-on: the reviewed run's manifest cites the focused gate as `result: pass` / `count: 4` with `log: negative-control.log`, but that file is the mutated arm: its own header reads '# mutation: reading timing from the first timestamped stream only makes completed_at read T1' and it ends '2 failed, 2 passed in 25.77s' / 'EXIT=1'. The passing run's own log is not cited anywhere, so a reader opening the named log sees the opposite of the claim. The claim itself is true — this review re-armed the same test file at 0bdce50f7 in a scratch extraction and got '4 passed in 45.47s' — so the defect is the citation, not the result.
